learning_objective: 🎯 Put your AI to the test! Learn the metrics used to check if a machine learning model is actually smart, or just making lucky guesses.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Just because an AI model is trained doesn't mean it works well. Evaluation is the process of testing the model against unseen 'Testing Data' to ensure it makes correct predictions in the real world without crashing.

It is a table that compares the AI's predictions with Reality. It has 4 quadrants: True Positive (AI said Yes, Reality is Yes), True Negative (AI said No, Reality is No), False Positive (AI said Yes, Reality is No), and False Negative (AI said No, Reality is Yes).

Accuracy measures overall correctness: (Total Correct Predictions / Total Cases). Precision measures exactness: Out of all the times the AI said 'Yes', how many were actually 'Yes'? (True Positives / All Predicted Positives).
Recall measures completeness: Out of all the actual 'Yes' cases in reality, how many did the AI successfully find? The 'F1 Score' is a single metric that perfectly balances both Precision and Recall.

fun_activity.title: 🚨 The Fire Alarm Matrix
fun_activity.instructions: Think of a Fire Alarm as an AI. True Positive: Fire happens, alarm rings. True Negative: No fire, no alarm. False Positive (Type 1 error): You burn toast, alarm rings (annoying!). False Negative (Type 2 error): House is burning, alarm stays silent (deadly!). Which error is worse?

exam_tips: 📌 Always draw the 2x2 grid for the Confusion Matrix. Reality on the top (Actual True/False), AI Prediction on the side (Predicted True/False).
📌 False Positives are also known as 'Type I Errors', and False Negatives are 'Type II Errors'. In medical AI (like predicting cancer), a False Negative is much more dangerous!
📌 Accuracy is a terrible metric if your dataset is highly imbalanced (e.g., 99% healthy people, 1% sick). In such cases, use the F1 Score.
quick_recap: ⭐ Evaluation proves the reliability and trustworthiness of an AI model.
⭐ The Confusion Matrix breaks down predictions into TP, TN, FP, and FN.
⭐ Precision, Recall, and the F1 Score provide deeper insights into a model's performance than basic Accuracy.
